functions.description: Parse the amount of substance in moles from raw question text, handling scale words and units with exact factors.
inputs: raw text giving the amount of substance with unit, e.g. 7.39 mol
outputs: amount of substance n in mol

functions.description: Parse the gas volume from raw text including its unit and convert it exactly to litres.
inputs: raw text giving the volume with unit, e.g. 0.03256 m3

functions.description: Parse the absolute temperature from raw text and convert it exactly to kelvin, applying the Celsius, Fahrenheit and Rankine offsets and scales.
inputs: raw text giving the temperature with unit, e.g. 507.15 K

functions.description: Provide the molar gas constant R expressed in L·atm/(mol·K) for use with volume in litres and pressure in atm.
Compute the ideal gas pressure p = nRT/V from amount, gas constant, temperature and volume using exact decimal arithmetic.
inputs: amount of substance n in mol
gas constant R in L·atm/(mol·K)
temperature in kelvin
volume in litres

functions.description: Cross-check an ideal gas pressure by recomputing nRT/V in SI units and comparing it with the primary pressure.
inputs: amount of substance n in mol
temperature in kelvin
volume in litres
pressure in atm

functions.description: Solve the ideal gas law pV = nRT for the pressure of a gas given its amount, volume and absolute temperature.
inputs: the amount of substance n of the gas with unit (moles)
the volume occupied by the gas with unit
the absolute temperature of the gas with unit
outputs: pressure of the gas in atm

functions.description: Parse a money amount text with an optional scale word into an exact decimal number of dollars.
inputs: raw money text with optional scale word such as million or k
outputs: money amount in dollars as an exact decimal

functions.description: Parse a text giving a count of years into a non-negative whole number of years.
inputs: raw text giving a count of years
outputs: count of years as an integer

functions.description: Compute the double-declining-balance depreciation rate as two divided by the useful life in years.
inputs: useful life in years as an integer
outputs: double-declining-balance rate as an exact fraction

functions.description: Compute one year of double-declining-balance depreciation as the rate times the opening book value, capped so the closing book value does not fall below the salvage value.
inputs: opening book value in dollars as an exact decimal
double-declining-balance rate as an exact fraction
salvage value in dollars as an exact decimal
outputs: depreciation for the year in dollars

functions.description: Simulate year-by-year double-declining-balance depreciation from cost up to a target year while keeping book value at or above salvage.
inputs: cost in dollars as an exact decimal
salvage value in dollars as an exact decimal
double-declining-balance rate as an exact fraction
target year as an integer
outputs: book value at the end of the target year in dollars

functions.description: Round a dollar amount to the nearest cent using half-up rounding.
inputs: dollar amount at full precision
outputs: dollar amount rounded to the cent

functions.description: Compute the book value at the end of a given year for a machine under double-declining-balance depreciation with a salvage floor.
inputs: the purchase cost of the machine in dollars, as written with its scale word or suffix (e.g. million or k)
the salvage value of the machine in dollars, the residual book value at the end of its useful life
the useful life of the machine in years
the target year at whose end the book value is requested, as a count of years since acquisition
outputs: book value at the end of the target year in dollars rounded to the cent

params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite number of moles (n > 0). Zero or negative amounts are physically meaningless. Parse scale words such as millimol or kmol with exact factors.

params.description: the volume occupied by the gas with unit

entry_points.text: A machine costs ●1, has a salvage value of ●2, and a useful life of ●3. Using double-declining-balance depreciation, what is its book value at the end of year ●4?

params.description: the purchase cost of the machine in dollars, as written with its scale word or suffix (e.g. million or k)
params.validity_range: A positive money amount. Must be strictly greater than the salvage value ●2, since otherwise there is no depreciable base. Scale words (thousand, k, million, bn, billion) must be converted to a full dollar amount before use.

params.description: the salvage value of the machine in dollars, the residual book value at the end of its useful life
params.validity_range: A non-negative money amount that is strictly less than the cost ●1. A salvage value of zero is valid and means full cost is depreciable. Book value is floored at this amount, so a salvage value equal to or above the cost makes depreciation meaningless.

params.description: the useful life of the machine in years
params.validity_range: A positive whole number of years. The DDB rate is 2 divided by this life, so it must be at least 2 to give a rate of 100 percent or less; a life of 1 gives a rate of 200 percent, which is not meaningful. Practically the life should be 2 or more years.

params.description: the target year at whose end the book value is requested, as a count of years since acquisition
params.validity_range: A non-negative whole number. Year 0 returns the cost itself. Values up to the useful life ●3 are normally asked; values beyond the useful life are not defined by the schedule and the book value would stay at salvage value after the asset is fully depreciated.
